stories.headline: Coatue Launches Next Frontier Venture to Buy Land for AI Data Centers Worth Tens of Billions

key_facts.fact: Coatue, Philippe Laffont's $70B investment firm, launched a new venture called Next Frontier in 2025 to buy land for AI data centers
Next Frontier has a joint venture with neocloud FluidStack that has raised $5.7 billion via junk bonds
Tens of billions of dollars could flow into the effort, with early construction work already underway on an Indiana campus
The facilities are intended for AI companies including Anthropic

stories.headline: FDA Approves First Non-Antipsychotic Drug for Alzheimer's Agitation, Affecting 76% of Patients

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Auvelity (dextromethorphan + bupropion) by Axsome Therapeutics for treating agitation in Alzheimer's dementia — the first non-antipsychotic approved for this condition.
Up to 76% of Alzheimer's patients experience agitation — including pacing, restlessness, and verbal or physical aggression — making it one of the most costly aspects of care.

In the Phase 3 ADVANCE-1 trial, Auvelity showed statistically significant improvement in agitation symptoms at Week 5 vs placebo, with only 1.3% discontinuation due to adverse events (same as placebo).
In the ACCORD-2 long-term study, patients continuing Auvelity experienced significantly longer time to relapse of agitation symptoms over 6 months vs those switched to placebo.
Auvelity received both FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and Priority Review for this indication; Alzheimer's disease affects more than 7 million Americans.

stories.headline: Google Rolls Out Gemini to Cars With Google Built-in, Replacing Google Assistant

key_facts.fact: Gemini is rolling out as a software update to both new and existing cars with Google built-in, starting with English in the US, replacing Google Assistant
Cars with Google built-in first hit the road in 2020; the update covers existing vehicles, not just new ones
Gemini integrates with manufacturer-provided owner's manuals to answer vehicle-specific questions like how to prepare for a car wash or adjust trunk height
GM previously announced Gemini is coming to approximately 4 million vehicles from model year 2022 and newer across Cadillac, Chevrolet, Buick, and GMC
Features include Gemini Live for free-flowing conversations while driving, Google Maps integration for contextual stop recommendations, and message summarization

stories.headline: Huawei Expects AI Chip Revenue to Hit ~$12B in 2026, Up 60%+ as Ascend Orders Surge

key_facts.fact: Huawei expects revenue from its AI chips to reach about $12 billion in 2026, up from $7.5 billion in 2025 — a jump of at least 60% — based on orders already received.
The majority of orders this year are for Huawei's latest Ascend 950PR processor, which entered mass production in March; an upgraded Ascend 950DT is planned for Q4.
DeepSeek's release of its V4 AI model on April 24, optimized for Huawei Ascend chips, triggered a procurement wave from Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent.
TrendForce forecasts the Chinese high-end AI chip market will grow by more than 60% in 2026, with domestically produced chips potentially capturing around half of that market.
Huawei's Ascend developer ecosystem now counts more than four million developers; 2025 group revenues were 880.9 billion yuan ($127.8B) with record R&D spending of 192.3 billion yuan.

stories.headline: Intel Stock Surges 114% in April, Best Month in Chipmaker's 55 Years on Nasdaq

key_facts.fact: Intel shares jumped 114% in April, lifting the chipmaker's market cap past $470 billion — by far the best month in Intel's 55-year history on the Nasdaq (previous best was 70% in July 1973).
Intel hit a record on April 24 for the first time since 2000, following a blowout earnings report with revenue up 7% to $13.6B — the biggest revenue beat in more than 5 years.
The rally is driven by Intel's 18A chips showing real promise at its new Arizona plant and surging CPU demand from agentic AI; Bank of America predicts the CPU market could more than double by 2030.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan said demand for Intel's data center CPU exceeds supply: 'The CPU is reinserting itself as the indispensable foundation of the AI era.'
The US government took a 10% stake in Intel in August, becoming its largest shareholder through an $8.9B CHIPS Act investment; that stake is now worth over $40 billion.

stories.headline: Intellia's CRISPR Gene-Editing Therapy Hits Phase 3 Win With 87% Attack Reduction, Begins FDA Filing

key_facts.fact: Intellia Therapeutics reported positive Phase 3 HAELO trial results for lonvo-z, the world's first in vivo CRISPR-based gene-editing candidate to produce Phase 3 data.
The primary endpoint was met with an 87% reduction in monthly attack rate (0.26 vs 2.1 for placebo) in patients with hereditary angioedema receiving a single dose of lonvo-z.
62% of lonvo-z patients were completely attack-free and therapy-free during the evaluation period, compared to 11% on placebo; 100% of lonvo-z patients achieved some attack-rate reduction.
The trial enrolled 80 patients with Type 1 and Type 2 HAE, randomized 2:1 to a one-time 50 mg dose of lonvo-z or placebo, with all adverse events mild or moderate.
Intellia initiated a rolling BLA filing with the FDA and aims for a commercial launch in the first half of 2027 if approved.
U.S. spending on chronic HAE medications is about $4 billion annually, with about 7,000 treated patients in the U.S. and more than 60% on long-term prophylaxis.

stories.headline: MARA Acquires Long Ridge Energy for $1.5B, Plans 1GW+ AI Data Center Campus in Ohio

key_facts.fact: MARA Holdings agreed to acquire Long Ridge Energy & Power from FTAI Infrastructure for approximately $1.5 billion (including assumed debt), gaining a 505 MW combined-cycle gas plant in Hannibal, Ohio, and over 1,600 acres of land.
The site could support more than 1 GW of total power capacity and increases MARA's owned-and-operated capacity by 65%, expanding its pipeline to roughly 2.2 GW.
MARA plans to begin construction on an initial AI and critical IT buildout in H1 2027, with first capacity targeted for mid-2028; the site has attracted interest from investment-grade AI tenants.
Long Ridge assets are expected to add approximately $144 million of annualized adjusted EBITDA at less than $15/MWh all-in operating costs.
CEO Fred Thiel: 'Power is the scarce input in AI' — the deal reflects the broader trend of bitcoin miners pivoting to AI data center infrastructure.

stories.headline: Musk Testifies xAI 'Partly' Used OpenAI Models to Train Grok via Distillation

key_facts.fact: During cross-examination on April 30 in Oakland federal court, Musk was asked if xAI distilled OpenAI's technology and said 'Partly'
Musk described distillation as standard industry practice, saying 'It is standard practice to use other AIs to validate your AI'
OpenAI's terms of service prohibit outputs from being used to train competing AI models
Musk ranked current AI providers: Anthropic #1, OpenAI #2, Google #3, Chinese open-source #4, characterizing xAI as much smaller with just a few hundred employees
The admission is notable because OpenAI and Anthropic have accused Chinese firms including DeepSeek of using distillation, but this is a rare public acknowledgment from a US-based lab

stories.headline: Nebius Acquires 20-Person Inference Startup Eigen AI for $643M to Boost Token Factory

key_facts.fact: Nebius agreed to acquire Eigen AI for approximately $643 million in stock and cash, valuing the 20-person startup at roughly $32 million per employee
Eigen AI specializes in maximizing the number of tokens each Nvidia GPU can generate during AI inference, using techniques like activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ)

Co-founder Wei-Chen Wang received the MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award for AWQ, now the standard for 4-bit model serving in production; co-founder Ryan Wang's SpAtten is the most-cited HPCA paper since 2020
Eigen AI's inference optimization layers will be integrated into Nebius Token Factory, its managed inference platform, which already ranked among the fastest on Artificial Analysis
The acquisition establishes Nebius's Bay Area engineering and research presence; the founding team includes MIT HAN Lab and CSAIL alumni
Inference is forecast to account for roughly two-thirds of AI compute demands in 2026

stories.headline: North Korea Stole $577M in Two Precision DeFi Hacks, Accounting for 76% of 2026 Crypto Losses

key_facts.fact: North Korean hackers stole approximately $577 million through the Drift Protocol ($285M, April 1) and KelpDAO ($292M, April 18) hacks, representing 76% of all crypto hack losses through April 2026.

The Drift Protocol attack involved months of unprecedented in-person social engineering, with North Korean proxies physically meeting Drift employees before draining funds in approximately 12 minutes.
The KelpDAO breach exploited a single-verifier design flaw in a LayerZero bridge; attackers compromised RPC nodes and launched a denial-of-service attack to drain ~116,500 rsETH (~$292M).
North Korea's share of total crypto hack losses has grown from under 10% in 2020-21 to 22% (2022), 37% (2023), 39% (2024), 64% (2025), and now 76% — the highest sustained share on record.
Cumulative North Korean crypto theft now exceeds $6 billion in attributed incidents since 2017, according to TRM Labs.

The KelpDAO theft triggered one of DeFi's largest wipeouts: $13 billion exited lending platforms in 48 hours, leaving Aave with a ~$200M bad-debt crisis now being backstopped by $300M in industry pledges.

stories.headline: Pentagon Signs Deals With 7 AI Companies for Classified Military Networks; Anthropic Excluded

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon reached agreements with SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Reflection, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services to deploy frontier AI on classified networks for lawful operational use.
The AI tools will be integrated into Impact Level 6 (IL6) and Impact Level 7 (IL7) classified network environments, the Pentagon's highest security tiers.
The Pentagon's GenAI.mil platform already has over 1.3 million users who have generated tens of millions of prompts and deployed hundreds of thousands of agents in five months.
Anthropic was excluded from the agreements after the Pentagon labeled it a supply-chain risk last month over a dispute about guardrails for military use of its AI tools.
The Pentagon described the agreements as accelerating its transformation toward becoming an 'AI-first fighting force' to maintain decision superiority across all warfare domains.
Oracle also joined the roster of companies later on Friday, bringing the total to eight firms deploying AI on classified networks.

stories.headline: Pentagon Signs Classified AI Deals With Nvidia, Microsoft, AWS, Google, SpaceX, OpenAI, and Reflection

key_facts.fact: The US Department of Defense entered agreements with seven companies — SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Reflection AI, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services — to deploy frontier AI on classified networks (IL6 and IL7).
The statement describes the effort as accelerating the transformation toward an 'AI-first fighting force' and strengthening warfighter decision superiority across all domains.
The Pentagon's AI platform GenAI.mil already has over 1.3 million users who have generated tens of millions of prompts and deployed hundreds of thousands of agents in five months.
The Pentagon finalized its agreement with AWS late Thursday; the announcement also marks the first official Pentagon confirmation of a new deal with Google reported earlier this week.
The push comes amid a dispute with Anthropic over safeguards on its Claude models, as the Pentagon seeks alternative AI systems for military use.

stories.headline: Russia Now Imports Over 90% of Sanctioned Tech Through China, Up From 80% Last Year

key_facts.fact: Russia now imports more than 90% of its sanctioned technology through China, up from about 80% last year, according to people familiar with internal assessments.
The sanctioned goods include semiconductors, integrated circuits, electronics, and machinery needed to produce weapons including missiles and drones.
Beyond components, China also provides Russia with geospatial intelligence, satellite imagery for military purposes, and drones, while restricting similar supplies to Ukraine.

EU sanctions against Chinese and Hong Kong companies accused of helping Russia circumvent restrictions have not had the expected effect, and most EU countries are not ready for tougher measures against China.
According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russia has spent approximately $130 billion over the past four years to circumvent Western sanctions and purchase banned goods.

stories.headline: Russia's New Soyuz-5 Rocket Aces Maiden Launch From Baikonur in First Debut in Decades

key_facts.fact: Russia's Soyuz-5 rocket lifted off for its first-ever flight on April 30 at 2:00 PM EDT from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on a successful suborbital test.
Roscosmos confirmed both first and second stages performed as planned, with a mockup payload launched onto the calculated suborbital trajectory before reentering over the Pacific Ocean.
Soyuz-5 was designed to replace Ukraine-built Zenit rockets — a critical need after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, severing access to Ukrainian rocketry expertise.
The Soyuz-5 can haul about 20 tons to low Earth orbit, comparable to SpaceX's Falcon 9 (25.1 tons), but is fully expendable with no reusable first stage.
The rocket has been in development since 2017 and launched from Site 45/1 at Baikonur, which was originally built for Zenit launches.

stories.headline: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Says AI Chip Substrate Demand Exceeds Capacity by 50%+, Begins Price Hikes

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electro-Mechanics said during its Q1 earnings call that demand for FC-BGA substrates used in AI servers and data centers currently exceeds its production capacity by more than 50%.
As AI chips grow larger in area, the number of FC-BGA units produced from a single wafer sharply declines, worsening the supply-demand imbalance.
The company is conducting price renegotiations with major Big Tech customers to reflect rising copper and gold raw material costs and the tight supply-demand situation.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics plans to more than double this year's capex vs. the prior year, concentrating resources on expanding capacity for high-capacity MLCCs for AI servers and substrates for AI accelerators.
The company launched a new 47uF MLCC product with double the capacity of existing 22uF products, targeting early lead in the AI server platform market.

stories.headline: SanDisk Q3 Revenue Surges 251% YoY to $5.95B on AI-Driven NAND Demand; Guides Q4 Up to $8.25B

key_facts.fact: SanDisk reported Q3 revenue of $5.95 billion, up 251% YoY and 97% sequentially, crushing the $4.72 billion estimate; adjusted EPS was $23.41 vs. the $14.62 estimate.
Datacenter revenue surged 233% sequentially; gross margin hit 78.4%, now higher than Nvidia's 75%.
SanDisk guided Q4 revenue of $7.75B–$8.25B with adjusted EPS of $30–$33, far above consensus.
SanDisk has signed three 'New Business Model' agreements with customers for multi-year supply backed by firm financial commitments, with two more signed in Q4.
Western Digital also beat estimates, reporting Q3 revenue of $3.34B (+45% YoY) and EPS of $2.72 (vs. $2.34 est.), guiding Q4 to $3.10–$3.40 EPS, citing AI-driven HDD demand.
